findings.title: canView(ClientModel) bypasses a client-specific negative permission
findings.body: canView(ClientModel) returns true immediately when canView() is true, and V2 canView() only evaluates the all-Clients resource for VIEW. If an administrator is granted VIEW on all clients but explicitly denied VIEW on one sensitive client through a negative policy on that client's resource, requireView(sensitiveClient) still passes. The client-specific denial is never evaluated, unlike canManage/canConfigure which evaluate the specific client resource, so the denied client remains directly viewable.

findings.title: Role-mapping checks do not imply manage or the manage-clients admin role
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only evaluate their exact FGAP scope and never fall back to canManage(client). An administrator with the MANAGE_CLIENTS realm role, or with a V2 MANAGE permission for the client (which canManage/canConfigure treat as the higher privilege), is therefore denied mapping that client's roles, composites, and client-scope roles. This is inconsistent with the manage > configure > view transitivity implemented elsewhere in this class and with the Users V2 behaviour where manage implies map-roles.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the all-Clients resource name as a client id
findings.body: resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients") also returns the synthetic all-Clients resource created by AdminPermissionsSchema.init, whose name is the literal string "Clients". When the caller has an all-clients grant, the returned set contains "Clients" instead of (or in addition to) real client UUIDs, and when only an all-clients grant exists no actual client ids are returned at all. Callers expecting a set of client ids to filter client listings will match nothing for the all-clients case. The synthetic resource must be excluded and an all-clients grant expanded to real clients (or handled by the caller).

findings.title: NullPointerException when the all-Clients resource does not exist
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists the code loads the all-Clients resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check (the String overload of hasPermission does check for null). getResourceTypeResource returns null whenever the Clients resource was never provisioned - e.g. realms whose admin-permissions client was created before the Clients type existed, since AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early when that client already exists - so every canView/canManage/canConfigure check for such a realm throws instead of returning false, breaking admin client operations with a 500.

findings.title: Listener still calls V2-unsupported methods when both FGAP features are enabled
findings.body: The listener is now guarded only by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but AdminPermissions.management()/evaluator() prefer MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature is also enabled. With both features on, deleting a client fires ClientRemovedEvent, passes the new guard, and calls MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which in ClientPermissionsV2 unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. The guard needs to also exclude the V2 case (or management() must not return the V2 implementation here), otherwise client deletion fails or logs an exception and the V1 cleanup is not performed.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type (returning "All users" or the username) and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Client resources created by getOrCreateResource are named by the client UUID and have no display name set, so authorization representations for the new Clients permissions will show a null/blank or raw-UUID name instead of "All clients" or the client's clientId. Add the analogous Clients branch resolving the client via session.clients().
